items.comparator: The source describes improvement from 51.82% selectivity; it does not specify a baseline procedure or comparator beyond that starting value.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article says the AI system pushed a single-step reaction’s selectivity from 51.82% to 85% in three months. It also reports a specialty-chemicals production-yield improvement from 72% to nearly 90%; comparator details for that project are not given.
items.signal: AI paired with an autonomous laboratory reportedly improved reaction selectivity and specialty-chemicals yield. The article describes the company’s closed-loop experimental data feeding back into its model, a possible copy-resistant capability, but the claims are company-reported and lack independent validation in the article.
items.source: ACCESS Newswire article republished by Yahoo Finance; reports Deep Principle’s claims.

items.comparator: The report says the speedup was in computational time but does not identify the baseline method or workload used for the 124× comparison. It separately says results were checked against established phaseless-AFQMC and full configuration-interaction references for stretched hydrogen chains.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article reports a speedup of up to 124 times in computational time for simulating battery materials; it attributes this figure to the company. It also describes scaling the method to a 40-qubit study of a lithium superoxide dimer rearrangement.
items.signal: Quantum-classical methods were applied to battery-material simulation, with a reported compute-time speedup and a 40-qubit study. The summary does not provide enough detail on the comparator or independent verification of the speedup to establish a measured operating advantage.
items.source: Quantum Zeitgeist report; attributes the speedup claim to IQM.

items.signal: AstraZeneca and Oracle announced a collaboration combining AstraZeneca’s scientific and clinical expertise with Oracle’s real-world data and AI-enabled clinical capabilities. The initial Abu Dhabi program is intended to help identify patients with uncontrolled hypertension, improve care, and support clinical-trial recruitment. This is a distinctive data-and-workflow partnership, but no measured benefit is reported yet.

items.quantitative_outcome: The article reports “cutting fit-for-use disposition decisions from three days to one minute” and “15–20% higher batch yields in biologics manufacturing.”
items.signal: A report on ParkourSC’s acquisition of Quartic describes outcomes attributed to the combined life-sciences supply-chain and manufacturing AI platform. These are operating-benefit signals, though the article does not give a comparator, study design, or identify a specific pharmaceutical customer for the reported figures.

items.comparator: Original estimated migration budget: AUD 70 million; revised cost was about AUD 35 million. The migration was completed more than two years ahead of schedule.
items.quantitative_outcome: The report says Westpac cut the estimated cost of its St.George data warehouse migration by half, to about AUD 35 million, and completed it more than two years ahead of schedule after engineers used AI for code conversion, testing, and documentation.
items.signal: AI-assisted legacy migration delivered a reported 50% reduction in estimated cost and a schedule acceleration; a potentially difficult-to-copy benefit given the bank-specific legacy code and engineering context.

items.comparator: Prior ability to take in submissions and quote them; no baseline, measurement method, or comparison group stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: The case-study article quotes CEO Rob Berkley saying the company’s “ability to take in submissions and quote them, is up by that 20%” where underwriting workbenches run. It also reports his earlier description of a “20-plus percent uplift in efficiency.”
items.signal: A reported improvement in underwriting submission intake and quoting, associated with workbenches deployed in a few operating locations; the proprietary implementation context may be harder to replicate than the tools alone.

items.comparator: Client transaction-data mapping previously took two and a half weeks; the agent reduced it to three days. First-pass quality was scored using an AI evaluation metric; the report describes a 96.5% score and human referral for uncertain cases.
items.quantitative_outcome: Microsoft’s article says, “Using the AI agent has slashed the time needed to map transaction data from new clients from two and a half weeks to three days.” It also reports a “96.5% FI first-pass quality score.”
items.signal: An AI agent reduced institutional-client transaction-data mapping time while retaining human review of uncertain items; the workflow’s client data and onboarding know-how could create a replicability barrier.

items.quantitative_outcome: “Within hours of using QuiltWorks, an EY Fortune 100 client identified nearly 45 million vulnerabilities, many undetected for years.”
items.signal: Project QuiltWorks, an industry coalition assessing and prioritizing frontier-AI risk, gave an EY client access to CrowdStrike SafeMind models and harnesses. The reported discovery yield is a potential weak signal: it suggests the combination of the tool and the client’s environment surfaced a large vulnerability backlog, but no baseline, validation method, or comparison is stated.

items.comparator: Compared with the network’s prior performance; the report gives no further baseline or test details.
items.quantitative_outcome: The report says initial testing found an 11% increase in 4G capacity and a 40% gain in user throughput during peak hours. No cost or accuracy outcome stated.
items.signal: Initial testing of a pre-commercial AIR RAN solution reportedly improved network capacity and peak-hour user throughput. The solution combines massive MIMO with AI-driven beam scheduling.
items.source: TelecomTV, reporting Ethio Telecom’s observation and citing a ZTE press release

items.comparator: Manual effort in fabrication planning; no numerical baseline, time period, or independent benchmark stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: Octave says the AI-based Fabrication Planner demonstrated the ability to “reduce manual effort by up to 60% while maximizing throughput.” It also says P&ID compliance checks that take engineers hours run in minutes on every revision; no quantified comparison beyond that description.
items.signal: AI and mathematical optimization are applied to MAIRE’s fabrication planning, alongside agentic AI checks on structured P&ID data. The engineering data and workflow integration could be harder to reproduce than a generic tool, but the outcome is reported by the vendor and lacks independent validation.
